The database name is rschema_0078, and it contains four tables: Author, Article, Author_creates_article, and Author_modifies_article.
The Author table has six columns: Author_ID, Email, Gender, Introduction, Name, and Phone. The Author_ID column is the primary key and is an integer. The Email, Gender, Introduction, Name, and Phone columns are all strings.
The Article table has ten columns: Article_ID, Article_collection_volume, Article_comment_volume, Article_content, Article_like_volume, Article_reading_volume, Article_title, Creation_time, Last_modification_and_save_author_ID, Last_modification_and_save_time, and Total_number_of_words_in_the_article. The Article_ID column is the primary key and is an integer. The Article_collection_volume, Article_comment_volume, Article_like_volume, Article_reading_volume, and Total_number_of_words_in_the_article columns are all integers. The Article_content, Article_title, and Creation_time columns are all strings. The Last_modification_and_save_author_ID column is an integer and references the Author_ID column in the Author table.
The Author_creates_article table has five columns: Article_ID, Author_ID, Author_order, Author_responsible_for_part, and Author_role. The primary key is a composite of Article_ID and Author_ID. The Article_ID column references the Article_ID column in the Article table, and the Author_ID column references the Author_ID column in the Author table. The Author_order, Author_responsible_for_part, and Author_role columns are all strings.
The Author_modifies_article table has five columns: Article_ID, Author_ID, Modify_notes, Modify_save_time, and Modify_start_time. The primary key is a composite of Article_ID, Author_ID, and Modify_save_time. The Article_ID column references the Article_ID column in the Article table, and the Author_ID column references the Author_ID column in the Author table. The Modify_notes and Modify_start_time columns are both strings.
In summary, the rschema_0078 database contains four tables that represent authors, articles, the relationship between authors and articles, and the modifications made to articles by authors. The database ensures data integrity through primary keys, foreign keys, and unique constraints.
gold_question: The article management system manages multiple articles. Each article has an article ID, article title, article content, creation time, total number of words, article reading volume, article like volume, article collection volume, article comment volume, the time of the last modification and save, and the author ID of the last modification and save. The system also manages multiple authors. Each author has an author ID, name, gender, phone number, email address, and introduction. Each article can be created by multiple authors, and the author order, responsible part, and role of each author are recorded. Authors can modify articles, and each modification records the modification start time, modification save time, and modification notes. The system ensures the accuracy of article content and the transparency of author contributions by recording article creation and modification information.

-- Schema for database: rschema_0078
CREATE TABLE `Author` (
  `Author_ID` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `Email` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `Gender` varchar(50) DEFAULT NULL,
  `Introduction` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `Name` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `Phone` varchar(50) DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`Author_ID`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `Article` (
  `Article_ID` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `Article_collection_volume` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,
  `Article_comment_volume` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,
  `Article_content` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `Article_like_volume` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,
  `Article_reading_volume` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,
  `Article_title` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `Creation_time` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `Last_modification_and_save_author_ID` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,
  `Last_modification_and_save_time` datetime DEFAULT NULL,
  `Total_number_of_words_in_the_article` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`Article_ID`),
  CONSTRAINT `article_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`Last_modification_and_save_author_ID`) REFERENCES `Author` (`Author_ID`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `Author_creates_article` (
  `Article_ID` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `Author_ID` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `Author_order` varchar(50) DEFAULT NULL,
  `Author_responsible_for_part` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `Author_role` varchar(50) DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`Article_ID`, `Author_ID`),
  CONSTRAINT `author_creates_article_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`Article_ID`) REFERENCES `Article` (`Article_ID`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `author_creates_article_ibfk_2` FOREIGN KEY (`Author_ID`) REFERENCES `Author` (`Author_ID`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `Author_modifies_article` (
  `Article_ID` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `Author_ID` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `Modify_notes` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `Modify_save_time` datetime NOT NULL,
  `Modify_start_time` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`Article_ID`, `Author_ID`, `Modify_save_time`),
  CONSTRAINT `author_modifies_article_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`Article_ID`) REFERENCES `Article` (`Article_ID`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `author_modifies_article_ibfk_2` FOREIGN KEY (`Author_ID`) REFERENCES `Author` (`Author_ID`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;
